args.summary: Completed the bytes-pattern support for the dynamic build's re engine in src/dynpy. The core port (Prog.bytes, bytes parsing rules with ASCII folding/classes, re_subject, bytes match/pattern reprs and attrs, pat_of/escape/sub/split/findall over bytes, and the LOCALE flag wiring in emit.rs/rt_enum.rs) was largely present in the working tree; I verified it against CPython 3.13 and fixed the remaining divergences: (1) re_compile2 now uses CPython's exact fix_flags order (bytes: UNICODE error first, then ASCII+LOCALE; str: LOCALE error first, then ASCII+UNICODE), so mixed flag ValueError messages match; (2) bytes patterns now raise "bad escape \N" for \N in atoms and character classes instead of "missing {"; (3) pat_call sub/subn was rewritten to CPython's order and laziness: template parsed before subject conversion, non-string replacements raise "decoding to str: ...", and a str/bytes template of the other type raises its TypeError only at the first match (no-match returns unchanged), with CPython's exact callable-result messages. Added a regression test tests/dyn/re_bytes.py (+ .expected). Verified with a wide range of CPython comparisons (compile/match/search/findall/split/sub/subn, ASCII/IGNORECASE/LOCALE rules, reprs, str/bytes mixing TypeErrors, escapes, templates, expand, scanner, flag combos); str-pattern behavior and performance paths are unchanged except where CPython correctness required it. Final check: 12/12 matched in both builds, no wrong answers, no cluster refusals.
